label: Theorem: main theorem for Links-Gould
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Theorem: main theorem for Links-Gould}
    If a link $L$ is obtained from links $L_1$ and $L_2$ by Murasugi-sum along genus-minimizing Seifert surfaces, then $$\mathrm{top}_{\text{LG}}(L,q)=\mathrm{top}_{\text{LG}}(L_1,q)\cdot\mathrm{top}_{\text{LG}}(L_2,q).$$
head: environment

label: prop: rearranged PBW
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Indeed, any usual PBW vector $K_1^{a_1}K_2^{a_2}F_1^{j_1}F_{12}^{j_3}F_2^{j_2}E_1^{i_1}E_{12}^{i_3}E_2^{i_2}$ is a linear combination of the reordered PBW vectors: this is because $E_1$ commutes with $F_2$, because $$F_{12}E_1=E_1F_{12}-[K_1]_qF_2+q^{-1}F_2[K_1]_q$$
   where $[K_1]_q=\frac{K_1-K_1^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}$ as it is readily checked, and because of the commutation relation between $E_1$ and $F_1$ (and because $K_i$'s commute with PBW vectors up to a power of $q$). By the same argument, the converse also applies. Since there is the same number of vectors in each degree (where we say $|E_i|=|F_i|=1$) and since $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}(2|1))$ is a free $U^0$-module (finitely generated in each degree), the lemma follows.

label: lem.simple
title: Lemma
body_md:
(\cite{Kac:reps})
\label{lem.simple}
The module $V(n,\alpha)$ has dimension $4(n+1)$. It is simple if and only if $(n,\alpha)$ is
typical, i.e. $\alpha(\alpha+n+1)\neq 0$. In particular, $V(n,\alpha)$ is simple when
$\alpha\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{Z}$.

label: lemma: ``cointegral'' cutting lemma
title: Lemma
body_md:
(Cutting lemma)
\label{lemma: ``cointegral'' cutting lemma}
    There exists a Laurent polynomial $\kappa(\alpha)\in \mathbb{Q}(q)[q^{\pm 2\alpha}]$ of the form $$\kappa(\alpha)=cq^{-2\alpha-1}+d+cq^{2\alpha+1}$$ where $c,d\in \mathbb{Q}(q)$, such that $$F_{12}F_{2}E_{12}E_{2}|_X=\kappa(\alpha)\cdot \overleftarrow{\text{coev}}_{V_{\alpha}}\circ\overrightarrow{\text{ev}}_{V_{\alpha}}+\overline{B}$$
    where $\overline{B}:X\to X$ is an operator whose coefficients (in the standard basis) are polynomials in $q^{-2\alpha}$ of degree $<2$.

label: remark: symmetry of kappa alpha
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{remark: symmetry of kappa alpha}
    For the proof of the main theorem it will be important to note that $\kappa(\alpha)$ has $\text{max-deg}_{q^{\pm \alpha}}=1$ and satisfies the same symmetry as the Links-Gould invariant of a link (namely, it is invariant under $p\mapsto p^{-1}$ if $p=q^{2\alpha+1}$.)
head: environment

label: remark: cutting lemma for root of 1 case is easier
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{remark: cutting lemma for root of 1 case is easier}
    The analogue of Lemma \ref{lemma: ``cointegral'' cutting lemma} for quantum groups at roots of unity (for any Lie type) was proved in \cite{LNV:Murasugi-sum} where instead of $F_{12}F_{2}E_{12}E_{2}$ one has $F^{I_{max}}E^{I_{max}}$ (there $E^{I_{max}}$ and $F^{I_{max}}$ are the top positive and negative PBW vectors). In that case, the module $X$ turns out to be a module over the small quantum group $\mathfrak{u}_q(\mathfrak{g})$, which is a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra hence has a (unique up to scalar) non-zero cointegral $\Lambda\in\mathfrak{u}_q(\mathfrak{g})$. In \cite[Lemma 5.9]{LNV:Murasugi-sum} it is shown that $F^{I_{max}}E^{I_{max}}$ acts on $X$ as the cointegral $\Lambda\in\mathfrak{u}_q(\mathfrak{g})$ up to lower degree terms. Then one can apply a result of \cite{CGPT} about cointegrals which essentially follows from the defining property of the cointegral and generalities about projective modules. The same argument cannot be applied for general quantum supergroups at generic $q$ since there is no finite-dimensional Hopf algebra to play the role of the small quantum group $\mathfrak{u}_q(\mathfrak{g})$.

label: prop: Seifert formula
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop: Seifert formula}
    If $\Sigma$ is a connected Seifert surface of a link $L$ built from an $N$-component tangle $T_{\Sigma}$ as above, then the Links-Gould invariant of $L$ is determined by $T_{\Sigma}$ as
    $$LG(L;q,q^{2\alpha+1})\cdot\text{id}_{V_{\alpha}}=(\text{id}_{V_{\alpha}}\otimes \overleftarrow{\text{ev}}_{V_{\alpha}}^{\otimes 2N})\circ(\overline{F}(T_{\Sigma},X)\otimes\text{id}_{V_{\alpha}})$$
    where $\overline{F}(T_{\Sigma},X)=\mathcal{J}_X\circ F(T_{\Sigma},X)$ is determined by left multiplication of the universal invariant $Z'_T$ acting on $X^{\otimes N}$ as in (\ref{eq: RT of T in terms of universal}).

label: prop: F(TS,X) as coev but upside-down
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop: F(TS,X) as coev but upside-down}
    Let $T_{\Sigma'}$ be a $N'$-component (framed, oriented) top tangle. Then the operator invariant $\overline{F}(T_{\Sigma'},X'):(X')^{\otimes 2N'}\to \mathbb{C}$ satisfies $$\overline{F}(T_{\Sigma'},X')=c'(q,q^{\alpha})\cdot\overleftarrow{\text{ev}}_{V_{\alpha}}^{\otimes 2N'}+B'$$
   \noindent for some $c'(q,q^{\alpha})\in \mathbb{Q}(q)[q^{\pm 2\alpha}]$ and a $B'$ with the following properties:
   \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
       \item $B'$ evaluates any standard basis vector of $(X')^{\otimes 2N'}$ to a Laurent polynomial in $q^{2\alpha}$ with $\text{max-deg}_{q^{2\alpha}}<N'$ and $\text{max-deg}_{q^{-2\alpha}}\leq  N'$.
       \item The coefficients of $\text{cl}(B')=(\text{id}_{V_{\alpha}}\otimes B')\circ (\overleftarrow{\text{coev}}_{V_{\alpha}}^{\otimes 2N'}\otimes\text{id}_{V_{\alpha}}):V_{\alpha}\to V_{\alpha}$
       satisfy $\text{max-deg}_{q^{\pm 2\alpha}}<N'$.
       \item $\text{max-deg}_{q^{\pm 2\alpha}}c'(q,q^{\alpha})= N'$ (except if $c'(q,q^{\alpha})=0$) and the coefficients of $q^{\pm 2\alpha N'}$ in $c'(q,q^{\alpha})$ coincide with the least/top coefficient of $LG(L';q,q^{2\alpha+1})$ where $L'=\partial\Sigma'$.
   \end{enumerate}
head: environment
labels: prop: F(TS,X) as coev but upside-down
